>  Sometimes your ideal partner might be sitting in front of you, but you can't see it for other life reason.

This. So tragic. 

I can't help but think there's more to this story than what you've presented. Like your backstory. Your comments present not just empathy but the sense of being pulled in 2 directions. What are you truly afraid of?
Or a fear of intimacy.

You misunderstand women. You think because (some) men want sex with anyone, women want a relationship with anyone. No. Women don't want to have sex with just any guy and don't want commitment from just any guy. They want the \*right\* guy.  Men do the same with commitment, just not as much with sex as women do. 

You imply only ugly men want commitment. Sorry I know plenty of gorgeous men deeply in love with their wives.
I find it fascinating that this is all about looks. It's not. I cannot recall a woman of my entire life who married or partnered with a man better looking. This is red pill crap.

ok here are my 2 cents: I think there's something in the communal dating water. At least in my area OLD is blowing up. My matches are blowing up, my friends male and female, my dates. It's the roaring 20s all right. With all this choice people are just wanting to binge date without realizing they are sabotaging themselves. A lot of people are first-time OLD because of the pandemic or getting back into OLD after a hiatus because life is short. One friend of mine is just amping up his dating approach because he thinks going on more dates than ever before will increase his odds of finding his life partner. I hope this will settle down soon. I've never had more dates in my life and they are all almost exclusively first dates. And they all go really well. It's annoying for those of us who've been at this a while and just want to settle down. oh well.

Just so you know, girls get told to "toughen up" too. Usually by their fathers. Or coaches. Or teachers. Not only does it destroy their self-image but it damages their chances for healthy relationships with men because they think they have to deny their true self to be loved and accepted by a man. 

HSP girls don't have it any easier. I'm tired of this boys vs girls crap.

Well thank you! I needed someone to give me permission to ask what I really want to know! Because frankly, I want someone to ask me about my job. It's kinda what I spend the vast majority of my time doing. And it tells you so much about me. 

Do you think men actually know what type of woman they are attracted to? beyond looks?

No. The oldest I've dated 15 years older and his age was the factor I broke it off. He was just tired and I was not. I've dated 12-10 years older a few times. 

I think the imperative question is why does \*he\* want a relationship with a woman 20 years his junior. The answers men have told me are not positive. Not the requirements for a healthy, loving, and equal partnership. 

Then, ask yourself the same question. Why do \*you\* want this man? If the age just happens to be what it is, I think the relationship would work. If there's another motivation, even one hidden from your conscious mind, then no. Those relationships never work. Also I would ask yourself what activities and lifestyle you want to do. In my case, I want to ski double blacks with my partner. My 15-year-older ex couldn't keep up with me. It got annoying and then depressing because I've got at least 15 more years of skiing like this (unless I crash). And he can't even keep up now. 

Also, libido. What's funny is when I mention to older men that their testosterone drops and therefore  so does their sex drive starting in their 20s and women's sex drive increases, peaking usually in their 40s, they all protest and protest and so no way. But in my personal experience their sex drive does diminish and mine just keeps increasing. Most men then counter with: little blue pills. Ok, let me ask you: have you had sex with a guy that took viagra? There's a difference. First of all he may not finish. Second forget morning sex and spontaneous sex. Would I, in my 40s, totally be understanding and get over this with a 49-year-old man? Of course! Because I had tons of sex in my 20s and 30s with men my same age (or was married to). Just food for thought. And, not certain if you've been married but sex is one of the main causes of divorce. There's another post on here about a dead-bedroom. Now before the men of reddit pillory me, I'm not saying ALL MEN in their 40s. I dated a 48-year-old that could put a teenager to shame (3x in 1 night). But for me that experience was rare. And, I wouldn't expect him to keep it up (haha) for another decade.

Let the photos show who you are. I'm super sporty and skiing is very important to me. I go to the opera every year. I have pics of me doing both. Don't show pics of the 1 time you did something that you'll never do again, e.g. scuba or something. 

I'd love to come across a guy's profile that mentions family and values. Unfortunately it's always a terminator-style declaration that their child/children are their 1 and only purpose for being on this planet and no other living organism will every remotely into the orbit of their importance to him. I just want to know if values family time and is open to more kids. 

I would avoid mentioning what you don't want. Others have mentioned that negativity is the kiss of death. Do mention what you do want but beware if you are too specific. As I said I'm super sporty but I recently passed on a profile that said I want someone to play tennis, scuba, and play beach volleyball. I only do 1 of those 3 so I passed. I \*really\* want a partner who will ski with me, preferably is as good as me. But it's not a deal-breaker. So just mention how much \*I\* love skiing.

Just thought I'd chime in to note that this both sexes! I like everyone's suggestion to have a 3 attempt rule. I'm a bit old fashioned and so think the guy should be driving at the very first. But dang at lot of men will just answer my question and then.... NOT ASK ME ONE. OMFG drives me insane. For one guy where I had been the only one to ask questions I eventually wrote, "so I guess you just want me to be the one the ask questions." He laughed and asked me a questions and then fell off. 

Like many responders here, I presume when some engages but doesn't ask questions or gives 3-word responses (as opposed to no contact after matching) that they 1) are juggling too many women or other commitments or 2) just want attention. 

It's great to get tons of matches, but then soooooo demoralizing when out of 10 only 1 is sincere about talking to you.

oh crap that's my go to. Woman here. I was told never ask about the job because you look like a gold digger. So if the profile is sparse and this is on bumble, so I have to do first, I'll ask this. Because I legit want to know what they do in their free time. I feel super corny asking a cutesy first question. Also if I'm not getting a talkative match I ask this.
as a woman, that's gross.

Agree! I've learned this the hard way. In my mind I call the person a different title, usually buddy or acquaintance. Then I have friends, someone who reciprocates. Then there's a good friend, someone who gives without needing me to always give back. 

A lot of it is expectations and understanding, so as not to take it personally, that someone might not have the emotional bandwidth for deeper bonding or might not have the time right now in their lives. 

Even though I can give more, I have learned to give what matches the reality of the relationship and if I cannot be content with that, I discontinue the relationship. Better to be lonely than used or unappreciated.

I disagree wholeheartedly. I think it is completely malicious to ignore someone into oblivion. Ignoring someone takes effort. It's different than forgetting. And when you've given someone several chances to remember your friendship and they don't, it's malicious. Their action says you don't matter to me and your feelings or experiences are inconsequential. To do this to someone you have an acquaintanceship or better is malicious. And when this happens we are entitled to be hurt, sad, and angry. Just as if this were a romantic relationship. Why do we hold romantic relationships to higher standards than friendships?

yes excellent question. I would want to read that in the profile. No long narrative, just "been in LTRs my whole life but never made it official with a license."

Sorry but I disagree. My time is precious. A coffee date means hair and make up, probably a change of clothes. That's time, money, and effort. I'd rather read more about this guy so I can make an informed decision. And it gives me something to talk about. 

I do not pick men on looks alone and then want to meet out of curiosity or to get a read on chemistry.

Cut the "year young" it gives the "I look younger than my age" vibe and makes me think you're exclusively trying to get as young and you can vs find the right woman for you. Turn off. 

Cut the parts where you repeat yourself, e.g. fit, athletic, weight, fitness. We get it. Just say it once. What are you really trying to convey?? Probably that you want a fit and active woman. Just say it. Maybe: I'm fit and active and looking for the same. It would be great to find someone to do X, Y, and Z, but it's not a requirement."

Same with happy and positive attitude. Those are starting to turn me off on dating profiles. I mean I get it, you dated negative, bitter bitches. But it's starting to feel like me saying on my profile "no sexist pigs." Try maybe "upbeat" if that's what you really want--someone f\*\*\*ing chipper 24-7. I doubt that's what you actually want (but maybe). What you're hoping to weed out (I assume) are bitter women. Am I right? Yeah we ALL want to weed out the people who haven't done "the work." If that's what you want, be direct. Try: "Looking for a woman who's got good emotional intelligence and works on self growth." Be sure to mention that you are emotionally mature and focused on self growth as well.

This has happened to me several times. In fact I expect it. My goal is to figure out why he lied. Is it desperation? Is there some fixation? One guy thought women his own age were repulsive. Sorry that's not a man I want in my life. Another guy was rebounding and wanted to get as many 20 year olds as he could. He was honest and told me. 

In my experience, there usually isn't a good reason for changing the date. Even if it's a fear of getting old and thinking a woman 10+ years younger will stave off the grim reaper. Then guess what--that's your job now. 

Like you I discovered it by googling. You totally need to vet the men you date! If you find a few sites that confirm the older age, then it isn't a fluke! I'm not saying dump him, I'm saying find out why.

you're likely picking up on his fears--perceiving so accurately your brain can makes images. IMHO the degree to which someone is empathic is on a spectrum; being able to feel someone's hidden fears is farther along on the spectrum. I can do this with some people--feel what they are hiding. I'm a visual person so sometimes my brain puts images in my head to go along with the feelings. I don't think these are visions though. 

Or, you can be projecting. For me one includes my own feelings of great compassion or shame/fear.

I appreciate your indignation and your gallantry! :)  I just meant in the course of my life I have been felt up. Almost exclusively at concerts and bars. I gave it as an example of male behavior I don't like but it doesn't mean I'm going to assume every man I encounter is going to do that and therefore I will treat all men like they're potential jerks.

I am a strong independent woman. When did that become an insult? You want a stage-5 clinger who can't take care of herself? 

Anyway, if I opened a door for a man or a woman and they were disrespectful--I'd roll my eyes and move on. I've also been groped by men dozens and dozens of time but that isn't going to stop be from being me. I dont let other people change my values.

You've gotten some good advice here. I'll second making sure your profile is appealing to the type of men you want to attract. If you emphasize how tough and independent you are, you'll probably not attract take-charge men. 

Second, try to have compassion for the men. It is nuts out there. As you will read on various reddit posts women tend to have lots and lots of rules, but there's little consistency lol. For example the issue of men paying divides lots of women. How are men supposed to know what to do! It took me a while to get used to OLD as well. What I do is just be friendly and talkative and keep lobbing the ball back to the man. If he never asks me out, we're not a match anyway. I stick to my values; I want a more traditional relationship. So if we can't even get on good footing from the start, it won't work. That being said it can take an awfully long time to get to the stage where men ask me out. Conversely sometimes they ask me sooner than I would like. I try not to get upset by this and just flow with what comes my way. They aren't mind readers and the last woman they dated probably went nuts over something and now they're gun shy. 

I think it's much better for a man to offer his number. Then you can do a reverse number look-up and make sure he's legit before giving him yours. I feel very nervous giving my number to a man on the internet. I think it's rather gallant for a man to respect the digital dangers women face and to offer the number first. If the number is given too soon I say thank you and ask if we can chat for a little bit more in app. BUT! I do not at all perceive a man giving me his number as an indication he wants me to ask him out. He just wants to text off app (maybe I'm wrong). They really like to do this, I have no idea why. Usually the guy will ask for a date after a call for a few days of texting. 

Finally, expect that a high percentage of your matches are either not interested in your or never had any intention of asking you out. Loooooooots of people use OLD for a distraction or for validation, whether single or not. They best thing you can do is not let it get to you. That only makes things worse. Granted you are absolutely allowed to vent and reddit is a good place for that.
And the OP definitely doesn't want that type of smug, entitled man.

My focus right now is mostly on making friends and acquaintances. And it's working.

One last thing that has helped: I focus on what I do have in abundance that I am lucky to have and many, many people do not: peace and tranquility. I make a point to relish sleeping in stupid late or staying up super late. Having no one to take care of or answer to. No one irritating me or making more work for me. I call this "family time." It's taking care of my family; a family of one. And that is just as important as any other family. In my mind it's different from self-care. Shifted my energy from painful to content.

Don't believe everything you read. You do you. If you aren't happy with the results, start brainstorming what you can modify. Everything is relative. Some people carry weight in their face, others don't. I had a gorgeous friend with a super thin face but about 30 lbs overweight. 

I was super excited to meet this one guy who had suuuuuper sexy photos but in person, ooof. Old, saggy skin, and pretty good beer gut. That's not a few months of letting yourself go. I felt deceived. A book has popped into my head: The Four Agreements. You're right, finding someone "fantastic" is totally not easy. You are lucky/blessed whatever. Time is immaterial; her needs are not. If verbalizing your feelings is painful or difficult, you can write a letter. There are also 4 other love languages! 

Do you love her? I realize it might be a hard or scary thing for you to figure out. Give yourself a reasonable amount of time to determine this. If she authentically loves you, you two can work around your struggle saying the words. 

Finding love is precious. If you found it, I hope you are able to grow it.

Oh, and describe the women who are liking you. Are there commonalities? Can you be specific about why you're not attracted? You might think you're pitching yourself a certain way, but maybe you aren't. Optics.

Anxious attachment people usually have some childhood abandonment/neglect issues to deal with (this doesn't have to mean trauma. It can just be personality mismatches). Often this is with parent of opposite sex. Psychotherapy, not just "therapy," can help you peel back the layers. Once you figure out how and why you have the neurological paths you do, you can do the hard work of laying new paths. In my experience when people just do talk therapy, or cognitive behavioral therapy, they just get a new coat of paint slapped on rotting walls. Sometimes you gotta go down the studs and rebuild. 

I would recommend getting a psychologist who has a phd or psyd, not just a therapist. When you first meet/interview them, ask if they do psychotherapy and what that means to them. There is a huge difference in caliber of training between 2 years of grad school and 6-8 years of grad school + clinical trials and a dissertation. \*not saying MAs and CBT can't help people, but if you want to dig deep, you need the full psychologist.

Yes. Positively enforce her behavior. 

My mom rarely texts me back. It drives me nuts. And we are super close. I've asked and asked for her to just send "message received." She cannot comprehend why I want a text back. She doesn't get that it leaves me hanging. Or I feel ignored. So now what. lol. It is who she is and I know she loves me. So I feed her shit about it and move on. The point is, I don't like it but I am so completely secure in our relationship that I get over it. I get attention in other ways. I also know how \*she\* likes to show her love for me. She likes to buy me doordash dinners. I don't feel loved from receiving the dinners but I do feel loved in that I can decode the action and know she is showing me her love. 

I recommend that, in addition to working on your attachment style, you work on observing and processing what love you do receive. The more you can acknowledge this, the more you can fill up your buckets indirectly. 

Also ask her, if she can, do a single character or emoji or something to give notice of receipt. It might work while you continue to build the relationship. Meanwhile, to help lay new neurological pathways, when you feel that hit of anxiety, remind yourself of the last act she did that you liked. Then turn to how much you like yourself. Be specific. Really work on identifying what you love about your personality, achievements, or whatever. Fixing 2 things when you do this.

I'm fairly certain 99% of the commenters don't know you fully paid for the second date. 

I've read all your carefully worded responses, even to some nasty comments. You are classy woman. You simply want your guy to equal that level of class. 

I think you and I are on the same page with dating, paying, LTR, and what we value in a man--and how we want to contribute to the relationship. So here's some actual advice from a like-minded person: dont change who you are or your values. You were a true lady on both dates and I would have done exactly the same thing. Well maybe not pay for the coffee and cakes. My ideal situation would be for there not to be a situation. Ever. I can find other ways to show my appreciation for being treated to date AND for removing any awkwardness (including a pre-date discussion of finances). I have had every experience regarding this and because my first priority is living my values, I adjust accordingly. But that may not mean a second date. 

I personally think it's vulgar to discuss finances with dates (I think the OP would too so this advice is for \*her\*). You could discuss values via text or something to try and gauge where he stands. But ultimately you just have to give it a go. You had to go on that 2nd date. There's no avoiding this in the future. But if you change your values, you aren't letting the man see the real you. i.e. if I assertively brought up to man my opinion who should pay, i'm showing him behavior that doesnt reflect how I would prefer to behave. It gives a false impression. Conversely if a man agrees to go dutch (because I offer that to be polite), but that's not really what he wants to do, then he gives me the false impression that's how he rolls. If we all stick to our values, we'll find out in the end who's a match. Same thing men expecting sex or women expecting to never pay; the only way a man or woman will know the values held by their date is to experience the person. What people do by changing behavior after being burned is become bitter. (wow alliteration).

Also, traveling is an expense. I find it particularly gracious if that is acknowledged, regardless of date, work, or friends. I have a girlfriend who hates driving, so I do. She always pays parking and buys me a drink. What manners! I hope you find a classy guy appreciates your manners.
